articles.title: Rupee retreats with stocks as rally takes a breather, positive bias lingers
articles.content: After a five-day rise, the Indian rupee faced a setback on Monday, driven by heightened dollar demand from major corporations. This shift in momentum was compounded by profit-taking activities. The rupee settled at 92.91 against the dollar, following a peak of 92.44. Additionally, underwhelming local stock performance fueled a bearish outlook for the rupee. Nevertheless, analysts predict a sustained positive sentiment towards stocks and currencies amid ongoing evaluations.

articles.title: German bond yields edge higher as equity rebound eases safe-haven demand
articles.content: Germany's government bond yields increased marginally on Monday as equity markets began to rebound, leading to diminished interest in safe-haven assets. In the wake of a difficult week for stocks, investors indicated a readiness to engage with riskier assets. The yield on 10-year German bonds rose by 2 basis points, signaling a fall in bond prices.

articles.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
articles.content: Indian government bonds fell after initial gains due to profit booking by traders and a sharp rupee decline. The benchmark yield of the 6.94% 2036 bond increased to 7.2185% during trading hours. Last week, the yield had dropped significantly due to lower US Treasury yields and a stronger rupee. Investors now focus on the upcoming Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.

articles.content: The Indian rupee initially rose to a seven-month high before retreating amid corporate dollar buying. Analysts noted that the rupee's early gains pushed it into overbought territory, prompting some selling. Despite recent fluctuations, the rupee has remained stable compared to other major currencies.

articles.title: The great Indian stock market comeback. Can the rally sustain and what should investors do?
articles.content: Indian equities staged a sharp 9.7% rally in eight sessions through November 12, reversing months of underperformance. A sell-off in US AI stocks, triggered by Republican losses in the midterm elections and fears of tighter AI regulation, spilled across global technology markets. Earlier, foreign investor outflows, elevated crude prices and rupee weakness had weighed heavily on Dalal Street sentiment.

articles.title: South Korean shares slump nearly 3% on AI-driven tech selloff despite policy pledge
articles.content: South Korean shares fell approximately 3% on Monday amid government efforts to stabilize the market. The KOSPI index dropped to its lowest level since January, raising investor concerns. Major technology stocks, including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, experienced significant losses during this decline. Authorities pledged to use stabilization funds but faced skepticism from investors regarding future returns. This situation reflects broader doubts about AI investments affecting global technology stocks.

articles.title: Dollar edges off 19-month high after market rout; yen softens
articles.content: The dollar has eased off its recent highs as positive investor sentiment rises. With traders dialing back their expectations for steep interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, the euro, Australian dollar, and several other currencies have exhibited modest recoveries against the USD. Following recent market volatility, prospects for a significant rate hike in December appear less likely. Meanwhile, cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ether, have seen slight downturns.
